newsitem.title: UK: Goldsborough buys two locum doctor services.
newsitem.headline: Goldsborough buys two locum doctor services.

text.p: Goldsborough Healthcare Plc said it acquired two firms providing locum doctor services for a total 4.4 million stg.
The two businesses had combined pre-tax profits of 0.68 million stg for the year to April 1996.
The acquisitions fit Goldsborough's strategy to create a diversified healthcare group.

Goldsborough earlier reported that full-year pre-tax profit fell to 4.2 million stg from 6.1 million after an exceptional charge of 1.3 million stg for its succesful defence against the bid earlier this year from Westminster Health Care Plc.
The pre-tax profit figure for the year to September 29 was also depressed by a first-time charge of 1.2 million stg for depreciation of properties.
Taking all charges into account, the full-year profits showed a solid performance, chief executive Graham Smith told Reuters.
"There is strong underlying growth," he said in a telephone interview.
Smith said he was particularly pleased with substantial increases in turnover and operating profits at the hospital and homecare divisions.
Hospital turnover rose 42 percent to 16.3 million stg, while operating profit increased 47 percent to 3.5 million stg.
Homecare turnover was up 64 percent to 27.1 million and operating profit surged 102 percent to 2.1 million stg.
Profit in care homes, however, fell six percent to 4.5 million stg.

With the exception of care homes, where market conditions remain difficult, all parts of the group were trading at substantially higher levels of activity that at the same time last year, Goldsborough said.
"We have two divisions showing good organic growth; we announced a major acquisition in the doctor locum business and we feel very confident about the future," Smith said.
